verified_behaviors: New omitted lifetime defaults to background; explicit connection inputs retain their canonical hashes. Execution metadata exposes immutable lifetime; historical responses without it decode as connection.
Closing a connection preserves only the exact pending background writer epoch. Original queue, writer and dispatch deadlines remain unchanged and no larger than the existing 30-second guarded budget.

Closed connections cannot renew, acquire, save files or submit new execution. Reconnecting cannot steal the reserved epoch. Valid original credentials retain owned query, replay and cancellation access.
Background mode does not bypass principal, credential, scope, grant, catalog, generation or Candidate checks. Revocation drains the writer; unknown dispatch never becomes a fabricated completion.

Real gVisor execution survives closure before dispatch and after its flushed start marker, completes with a live process/IO seal, retains output.txt and supports authenticated output downloads. Completion acknowledgement retry succeeds with the same seal after disconnect.
A third background task is detached, then explicitly cancelled by checkpoint-stop; capture waits for physical drain, and a fresh Candidate restores started.txt without late.txt.

Independent SQL verifies immutable lifetime, closed sessions, exact deadlines, terminal outcomes and event chronology. Separate signed S3 reads and readonly JuiceFS clients verify output and restored bytes.
experiment_notes: No repo-sandbox targets were registered and WSL is unsupported; used the authorized disposable QEMU fallback with 4 vCPU, 6 GiB RAM and a 24 GiB overlay.

Focused tests initially exposed fixture issues: a wrong catalog table name, an HTTP replay assertion expecting 200 instead of existing queued 202, and an App-enabled fixture in a file-only checkpoint test. Corrected the fixtures without relaxing production authority or stop rules.
The first manual Bazel build omitted the new helper from explicit srcs. Added it and reran the full default targets and all eight manual builds successfully.
The supervisor OCI image was reused after verifying its unchanged source-bound binary hash.

One repeated VM execution run failed to observe the output-unknown start marker. SQL showed no accepted watchdog record or startup grant, with Unknown/Draining and no completion. The two local guard journals recorded deadline/Unknown/KillFailed, and the Pod was absent when inspected; this does not identify the original pre-grant failure. Added diagnostic output for this fixture precondition and repeated validation without relaxing any runtime check. The failed attempt is retained separately and is not counted as a pass.

The first VM run passed. The final OpenAPI connection-close description changed the embedded server binary; rebuilt it and rechecked server contracts. The repeated Candidate fixture first collided with the prior retained local spool directory (DirectoryNotEmpty); configured a distinct private spool and reran both real fixtures with the final binary before collecting evidence. The failed attempt is not counted as a pass.
limits: One Linux VM with isolated HTTP object transport; no production TLS, HA, cross-node, load, throughput or power-loss certification.
Background is a logical-disconnect policy within the existing fixed budget, at most 30 seconds. Longer jobs and renewable worker-owned execution budgets remain pending.
Original credential/grant/catalog loss and deadline exhaustion remain blocking. Restart or a new credential cannot recreate a live completion seal or replay a dispatch.
Checkpoint stop still rejects declared Apps and blocking active use; general process draining, App/browser checkpointing and storage GC remain incomplete.
Computer ready=false; public execution unsupported. Full lifecycle scheduling, runtime/App health, browser/ComputerView and T01-T43 product acceptance remain incomplete.
